answer: Admission is capped at 6 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm hence spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the reef quota and the timber admission check. Because the quill audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 5 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
